Ordinal models in table_regression()

Source: R/table_regression_ordinal.R
table_regression_ordinal.Rd

table_regression() reads the cumulative-link models of MASS::polr() and ordinal::clm(), and the cumulative-link mixed models of ordinal::clmm(). The predictor coefficients fill the rows, as proportional odds ratios under exponentiate = TRUE with the logit link. The cut-points follow them as a Thresholds block of rows, and the partial-proportional-odds terms of a clm fit as a Non-proportional effects block. A clmm fit adds the Random effects block of the mixed models, described in table_regression_mixed, as does glmmTMB::glmmTMB() with family = glmmTMB::ordinal(), which follows the rules of this page for its thresholds. The ordinal fits of survey::svyolr() and rms::lrm() take the same Thresholds block.

Usage

table_regression(
  models,
  show_thresholds = TRUE,
  show_components = TRUE,
  ...  # the arguments of every class: see ?table_regression
)

The other arguments are documented in table_regression(); the values they take for ordinal models are listed below.

Engines

ClassEngineAMEExponentiateBlocksvcov
polrMASS::polr()per categoryOR (logit)Thresholdsclassical, CR1
clmordinal::clm()per categoryOR (logit)Thresholds; Non-proportional effects (nominal =); Scale effects (scale =)classical, CR1 (classical only with scale or nominal terms)
clmmordinal::clmm()noOR (logit)Thresholds; Random effectsclassical

AME: whether the average-marginal-effects columns are available; per category is the marginal effect on each probability \(P(Y = k)\). Exponentiate: what exponentiate = TRUE gives. Blocks: the labeled blocks of rows the class adds below its coefficients. vcov: the values of vcov the class accepts. The same rows are returned by subset(table_regression_models(), family == "Ordinal").

What the table shows

Coefficient rows. One row per predictor coefficient, on the log-odds scale under the logit link. Under exponentiate = TRUE they are proportional odds ratios (logit), or hazard ratios of the grouped event under the cloglog link (see exponentiate below).

Thresholds. The cut-points render as a Thresholds block, with B, SE, CI and p like the predictor rows (show_thresholds). They are reported on the log-odds scale and never exponentiated.

Non-proportional effects. The terms of a clm fit given in nominal = (partial proportional odds) render as a Non-proportional effects block, one coefficient per cut-point. The covariate effects of scale = render as a Scale effects block (show_components).

AME. Per category: the marginal effect of the predictor on each \(P(Y = k)\), for polr and clm fits.

Fit statistics. By default, n, McFadden's pseudo-R-squared and AIC. See R-squared of glm and categorical models in table_regression().

Arguments for this family

show_thresholds

Logical. TRUE (default) displays the cut-points as a Thresholds block of rows below the predictors, carrying B, SE, CI and p like the predictor rows. FALSE collapses them to a one-line note instead. Thresholds are reported on the log-odds (B) scale and are never exponentiated. They follow the polr convention, link(P(Y <= j)) = threshold - linear predictor: an rms::lrm fit, which models P(Y >= j), shows its intercepts with the sign reversed, named "3|4" (displayed "3 | 4") rather than "y>=4". The rows are shown only when a coefficient column ("b" or "beta") is in show_columns; otherwise the cut-points go to the note. Applies to polr, clm, clmm, svyolr, glmmTMB with the ordinal family, and rms::lrm with more than two outcome levels.

show_components

Logical. TRUE (default) displays the scale = ~ effects of a clm fit as a Scale effects block: the covariate effects on the log standard deviation of the latent response. They are never exponentiated: their exponential is a ratio of latent standard deviations, not an odds ratio. FALSE omits the block. The argument also governs the zero-inflation and hurdle blocks of the count models (table_regression_counts).

The arguments shared with other classes take these values for ordinal models:

vcov, cluster

polr and clm: "classical" and "CR1". A clm fit with a scale or nominal component, and clmm: "classical" only. See Standard errors, degrees of freedom and intervals.

ci_method

"wald" or "profile" for polr and clm: "profile" uses confint.polr() or confint.clm() for the predictor coefficients; the thresholds stay Wald. Only the bounds change: the estimate, SE, statistic and p-value remain Wald. A robust vcov takes precedence: its Wald intervals are used, with a warning. clmm takes "wald" only.

exponentiate

Odds ratios under the logit link. Under the cloglog link, the displayed HR is exp(-B), not exp(B): the cumulative parametrization cloglog P(Y <= j) = zeta_j - xB places the hazard of the grouped event on -B, so exp(B) would be the reciprocal of the hazard ratio. The CI endpoints are negated and swapped accordingly, and the note states the convention. A cloglog clm with nominal = terms refuses exponentiate, because threshold-side coefficients have no covariate-HR reading. Other links (probit, cauchit, loglog) refuse it. A clmm fit with the cloglog link and a single random intercept refuses it too: on the current ordinal, clmm() fits such a model with the loglog link, and the reverse.

standardized

Refused: an ordinal outcome has no scale to standardize.

show_columns

The AME tokens give one effect per category for polr and clm; clmm refuses them.

Standard errors, degrees of freedom and intervals

The coefficients and thresholds are tested by Wald z. Cluster-robust variance is "CR1", from sandwich::vcovCL(): the CR0 sandwich scaled by \(G/(G-1)\), G the number of clusters, the one cluster estimator of these classes; "CR0", "CR2" and "CR3" are refused rather than mapped. The thresholds take their uncertainty from the same clustered matrix. A clm fit with a scale or nominal component has no estimating functions in ordinal for those parts, so no sandwich can be built for it.

Hierarchical comparison (nested = TRUE). Nested polr or clm fits are compared by likelihood-ratio test, c("lrt_change", "p_change"); under "CR1" the change test is the Wald chi-square of the added coefficients on the robust matrix. See Hierarchical (nested) model comparison in table_regression().

Fit statistics

polr, clm and an ordinal rms::lrm default to c("nobs", "pseudo_r2_mcfadden", "aic"). "nobs" and the BIC follow the engine's stats::nobs(), which for a weighted polr or clm fit is the sum of the weights. The deviance R-squared is refused for ordinal models, where it equals McFadden's. Cumulative-link mixed models show the fit statistics of the mixed models (n, groups, AIC, BIC), without an R-squared; see table_regression_mixed.

Cumulative-link mixed models

ordinal::clmm() fits, and glmmTMB::glmmTMB() fits with family = glmmTMB::ordinal(), keep the Thresholds block and add the Random effects block described in table_regression_mixed. Their inference is Wald only: the AME columns, a robust vcov, ci_method = "profile" and standardized are refused, as is nested = TRUE for clmm. The random-effects likelihood-ratio test of the note refits its null model with the link actually fitted.

What is refused, and why

  • HC*, "bootstrap", "jackknife", and the CR* tokens other than "CR1": "CR1" is the one robust estimator of these classes.

  • A robust vcov for a clm fit with a scale or nominal component, and for the cumulative-link mixed models.

  • exponentiate = TRUE under a link whose exponential is not a ratio, and in the cloglog cases above.

  • standardized, for every class of this family.

  • For the cumulative-link mixed models, the AME, ci_method = "profile", and nested = TRUE for clmm.

See also

table_regression() for the arguments shared by all classes; table_regression_models() for the registry of supported classes and the other families; table_regression_mixed for the random-effects rows of clmm and of the ordinal family of glmmTMB; table_regression_survey for survey::svyolr(); the Ordinal regression tables article.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("MASS", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- MASS::polr(Sat ~ Infl + Type, weights = Freq,
                    data = MASS::housing, Hess = TRUE)
  print(table_regression(fit, exponentiate = TRUE))

  # Cut-points in the note instead of a block of rows.
  print(table_regression(fit, show_thresholds = FALSE))
}
